title: On the sum of a prime and a square-free number
abstract: Conditional on one explicit hypothesis, AP12Lower 0.21, taken as a hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom: for every integer x >= 10^9, each reduced residue class mod 12 holds more than 0.21 x / log x primes p <= x. Under it, a complete Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. W. Dudek, On the sum of a prime and a square-free number, The Ramanujan Journal 42, 2017: every integer N > 2 is the sum of a prime and a square-free number. AP12Lower 0.21 is implied by Corollary 1.6 of M. A. Bennett, G. Martin, K. O'Bryant and A. Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions, Illinois J. Math. 62, 2018, which gives 1/4 in place of 0.21; the entry proves that implication in Lean, with the corollary itself stated as a hypothesis. The even case, every even N >= 4, is proved with no hypothesis. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
